findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === never equal
findings.body: At line 114 the code does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a zero-length date override (unavailable day). Dayjs instances are objects, so `===` compares identity and is always false. As a result a full-day block is never detected, `find` returns falsy, `dateOverrideExist` stays true and the function returns `true` (available). Unavailable date overrides become bookable.

findings.title: Wrong dayjs.tz overload for UTC offset
findings.body: Line 107 computes `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`. That overload parses `date.start` as wall-time in `organizerTimeZone` instead of converting the instant to that zone. The correct form is `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`. The current code yields a bogus offset (dependent on system TZ and double-interpretation), so date-override day matching and in/out checks are shifted by hours.

findings.title: Working-hours end ignores event length and rejects valid slots
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable` both `start` and `end` are computed as `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. `eventLength` is never added, so slots that overflow `workingHour.endTime` are accepted. Worse, the `find` returns true if ANY `workingHour` entry for the day does not contain the slot. With split hours or multiple entries a slot contained in one entry but not another is incorrectly marked outside working hours and filtered out.

findings.title: Working-hours / date-override checks use UTC instead of organizer TZ
findings.body: `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()` and checks use `slotStartTime.day()/hour()/minute()` and `format('YYYY MM DD')` in UTC. `workingHours.days/startTime/endTime` and override dates are defined in organizer/schedule timezone. Near midnight or with non-UTC organizers the UTC weekday/hour maps to the wrong working-hours entry, accepting slots outside hours and rejecting valid ones.

findings.title: Date-override day filter ignores timezone shift
findings.body: Line 207 selects `activeOverrides` by `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, ...)` without converting the override instant to invitee wall-time. An override that belongs to a date in organizer TZ but falls on an adjacent UTC/invitee day is either dropped or applied to the wrong `inviteeDate`, so overrides disappear or leak, and the later hour/minute-only conversion cannot recover the day shift.

findings.title: Override TZ conversion unsafe when timeZone missing, drops day overflow
findings.body: Lines 212-223 do `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` where `TimeRange.timeZone` is optional, so `tz(undefined)` can throw or fall back to system TZ. It also reduces times to `hour()*60+minute()`, discarding the date. If the organizer-to-invitee offset pushes the override past midnight, start>end or wrong-day values are used and `buildSlots` skips them (`start>=end` continue), yielding zero slots instead of shifted slots on the correct day.
